cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Need Your Blessing
cards.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Dad, I've accepted the museum job. Can you be pleased I'm leaving the workshop?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're thirty. You don't need me to release you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I need the person who taught me to make things to think this counts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pack your tools. You might want to come back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you sharpen them for the museum instead? Send me off expecting me to do well.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 status prefixes do not change the actual vulnerable request for Dad endorsement; A5 could you sharpen is ordinary pleading rather than superior direction.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 no release needed prompts A3 teacher opinion distinction; B4 fallback tools prompts A5 forward-looking preparation, a strong Drive chain.

relationship.evidence: B2 recognizes adult autonomy and B4 offers a fallback, making the father concerned rather than arbitrarily withholding.

heightening.evidence: B4 packing for possible return causes A5 request to sharpen for the museum, a concrete version of belief in success.

specificity.evidence: A1 museum job/workshop departure and B2 adult age establish that permission is unnecessary; A3 teaching explains emotional weight.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 tools for success is earned, but stock A3 authority phrase disrupts its sincere mechanism rather than changing it.
